turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I am not cowed by your bravado, Sandip. The safety of my people and land is my foremost concern, and I will not hesitate to act in their defense.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Nikhil, your concern for your tenantry's safety is as theatrical as your speech. But let me assure you, your tenants are not oppressed; they are inspired. As for the Mussulmans, they are mere shadows cast by your own fears. But if you insist, I will leave your territory, for now. Your request is granted, but remember, the spirit of the people cannot be contained.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your theatrics may amuse others, Sandip, but they will not sway me. I will not tolerate any further interference with my people, and I suggest you act on your promise.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, Nikhil, you wear the mask of the protector, but your heart is that of a skeptic. I leave your lands, but let it not be said that I fear your walls. The spirit of freedom I sow will find its way through the cracks of your fortress.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your words may be grand, Sandip, but your actions speak louder. I trust you will keep your promise, or the consequences will not be favorable for you.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Very well, Nikhil. I depart from your lands, but remember, the seed of revolution is small, yet mighty. It grows without fear, and it shall bloom where the soil is fertile.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your departure is noted, Sandip. But do not think for a moment that I will be idle. I will ensure your seed of revolution finds no fertile ground on my land.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: I see the fortress walls, Nikhil, but I also see the cracks where the seed of change can slip through. Your tenants may not be as loyal as you think.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your words may plant seeds, Sandip, but my actions will ensure they do not take root. I will keep a close watch on my people, and any who seek to sow discord will answer to me.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: The people, Nikhil, are like rivers. They flow where the path is clear. And if you obstruct them, they will find another way. Beware the strength of the current.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your metaphors are as dangerous as they are poetic, Sandip. But let it be known that I will not stand idly by while you poison the minds of my tenants.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Poison the minds? More like lighting a fire under their feet. They thirst for change, Nikhil, not just a breath of fresh air.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your rhetoric may be stirring, Sandip, but it is the actions of men that shape the world. I demand you cease your disruptive influence or face the consequences.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh Nikhil, ever the voice of reason and restraint. But tell me, do you truly believe the tide of progress can be held back by mere walls and threats?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Progress is not a tidal wave, Sandip. It is a journey built on the foundations of stability and justice. I will not allow you to incite my people against me.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: The walls you speak of, Nikhil, are nothing but the crumbling remnants of an outdated order. Stability is a cage for the spirit, and justice is a mirage in the desert of your complacency.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Stability is not a cage, Sandip, but a sanctuary for the oppressed. Your words may inspire, but they also sow discord and fear. Enough is enough.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Discord and fear? Nikhil, you speak of stability, but it is the fire of change that will light the way to a new dawn.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Your rhetoric is stirring but misguided, Sandip. It is one thing to inspire, quite another to manipulate. Cease your divisive tactics or face the consequences.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, Nikhil, always so cautious, so predictable. But fear not, my friend, for the tide of change cannot be stemmed by the narrow-minded. Let us hope that your tenants find their own path to enlightenment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ... No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
